sources.title: USDA NASS Quick Stats: WHEAT, WINTER - PRODUCTION and ACRES HARVESTED, Iowa, state (Census of Agriculture 2022)
sources.locator: yield: 2022 Census, Iowa winter wheat 934,915 bu from 14,944 acres harvested = 62.56 bu/acre, our calculation; converted with 60 lb/bu, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, 1 acre = 0.40468564 ha. sources.title: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker File A1-20: Estimated Costs of Crop Production in Iowa - 2026 (FM 1712, revised January 2026)
sources.locator: direct costs: page 10, Annual Production Costs for Established Alfalfa or Alfalfa-Grass Hay, 4 tons per acre column, "Total fixed and variable cost using large round bales per acre", variable part $242.56/acre. The page has two columns, 4 and 6 tons per acre; the 4-ton column is the closest to the Iowa mean of 3.68 short tons/acre (0.32 t away, the 6-ton column 2.32 t). We do not scale it down to 3.68: the page gives no budget below 4 tons, and stretching the 4-to-6-ton slope below its range would be our estimate, not ISU's. Fertiliser and harvest costs grow with tonnage, so the cost is a little high for 3.68 tons and the margin a little low. Establishment costs (page 9) are not included; divided by 0.40468564 ha/acre

sources.title: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker File A3-10: 2026 Iowa Farm Custom Rate Survey (PDF of March 2026)
sources.locator: direct costs: operations only, seed not included (no ISU/USDA seed price found, R9 Missing). p. 1, "Planting, Drilling, and Seeding", row "Drilling cover crop seed", Average $19.05/acre (sowing in late summer or fall); p. 2, row "Ground, broadcast, not incorporated, self-propelled", Average $9.35/acre (one spraying pass to end the cover crop in spring; the herbicide itself is not included); $28.40/acre divided by 0.40468564 ha/acre = 70.18 USD/ha (our calculation; 47.07 + 23.10 USD/ha). Custom rates are what a farmer pays a contractor, so they include machinery, fuel and labour
